questions.q: What is the large cavity lined by dark cells called?
options: The antrum of an antral follicle
The lumen of a seminiferous tubule
questions.explain: An antrum is the fluid-filled space within a developing antral follicle.

questions.q: A section of the ovary shows a large follicle with an antrum, granulosa-cell layer and an eccentrically placed oocyte. At what stage is this follicle?
questions.explain: The fluid-filled antrum is the defining feature of an antral or secondary follicle; the oocyte is surrounded by granulosa cells and the follicular wall is organised into theca layers.

questions.q: Which cells form the granulosa layer surrounding the developing oocyte in an ovarian follicle?
questions.explain: Granulosa cells are derived from follicular epithelial cells and surround and support the oocyte; they also participate in oestrogen synthesis.

questions.q: After ovulation, the ruptured ovarian follicle is transformed into which temporary endocrine structure?
questions.explain: The granulosa and theca interna cells luteinise after ovulation to form the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone and some oestrogen.

questions.q: A uterine section in the secretory phase shows tortuous glands with luminal secretions and oedematous stroma. Which hormone is chiefly responsible for these endometrial changes?
questions.explain: Progesterone from the corpus luteum converts the oestrogen-primed endometrium into a secretory lining suitable for implantation.

questions.q: Which epithelial lining is characteristic of most of the uterine tube and is important for movement of the oocyte?
options: Simple columnar epithelium containing ciliated and secretory cells
questions.explain: The uterine tube is lined by simple columnar epithelium with ciliated cells that help move the oocyte and secretory peg cells that provide a supportive fluid.
